title: Retention schedule by record class, legal basis and enforcement
status_rationale: CNV-PLT-004 sets a design retention schedule (10-year floor for transaction-level financial and grant records, permanent for organizing documents, legal-hold precedence, sponsor approval). SOC2-023 warns against inventing universal retention periods. The 10-year floor is a design decision informed by sanctions record rules, not a finding that law requires 10 years for every record class.
target_answer: Each tenant has a retention schedule by record class, approved by the sponsor's compliance owner and counsel, with the legal or business basis recorded per class. Unbound ships a default (CNV-PLT-004) the sponsor can lengthen but cannot shorten below documented legal minimums. Disposition runs automatically when a record's retention ends and no hold applies, and each run produces an evidence record. Records of closed funds and deceased donors follow the same schedule.
current_practice: Not established. A design schedule exists in requirements; no counsel review or sponsor approval has occurred.
intended_practice: Obtain counsel review of CNV-PLT-004 per record class; implement schedule as tenant configuration with floor checks.
provable: Requirement text only: CNV-PLT-004 in unbound@9b38de47.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify a default retention schedule that the sponsor's compliance owner approves, with legal holds overriding disposition. The default periods have not yet been reviewed by counsel. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
owner: Records and retention owner (proposed role; not appointed)
open_questions: Which CNV-PLT-004 retention periods are legally required, which are conservative defaults, and which are unsupported? Counsel review required.
How should retention apply to personal data in records whose financial retention period has ended but whose sponsor is in an IRS examination?

title: Legal holds
status_rationale: CNV-PLT-004 gives legal holds precedence over disposition; SOC2-006 and UNB-GAP-019 call for legal hold design. Nothing is built.
target_answer: Legal holds are first-class records scoped to a tenant, fund, person, grant, case or date range, placed and released only by authorized sponsor or Echelon counsel roles. A hold suspends disposition and deletion (including rights-request erasure) for records in scope, and the conflict is reported to the requester's handler. Holds, scope changes and releases are logged immutably.
intended_practice: Implement holds as records evaluated by the disposition and erasure services.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify that legal holds override disposition. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.

title: Deletion and media sanitization in a cloud service
status_rationale: UNB-DATA-007 names documented cryptographic erasure where lawful; UNB-IMM-008 forbids claiming crypto erasure works where plaintext persists. No hosting provider is selected, so no provider sanitization attestation exists.
target_answer: Logical deletion is completed by cryptographic erasure of per-tenant and per-person keys, which NIST SP 800-88 recognizes as a sanitization technique when keys are strong and fully destroyed. Physical media sanitization is the hosting provider's responsibility, covered by its independent attestation that Echelon reviews annually. Endpoints that may hold customer data are full-disk encrypted and sanitized by crypto erase plus device reset on retirement. Deletion completes in primary systems within 30 days of the triggering event and in backups by expiry (see ANS-RET-004).
current_practice: Not established. No hosting provider or key management service selected.
intended_practice: Select provider and key service; document the sanitization approach per storage type.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify cryptographic erasure where lawful, without claiming it works where plaintext copies remain. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
open_questions: Which hosting provider will be used, and what does its current attestation say about media sanitization?
Does the current revision of NIST SP 800-88 change the treatment of cryptographic erase relative to earlier revisions? Verify before citing a specific section.

challenge.customer_intent: Customer wants assurance that deleted data cannot be recovered.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Recovery of deleted donor data from reused media, snapshots or decommissioned devices.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Physical destruction certificates are meaningful for owned media but not for multi-tenant cloud storage the vendor never touches.
challenge.legally_required: Disposal of customer information is required under the FTC Safeguards Rule for covered financial institutions; otherwise contractual.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly requested, often with a demand for NIST SP 800-88 conformance.
challenge.historical_convention: Media sanitization practice predates cloud; questionnaires still ask about degaussing and shredding.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Per-tenant and per-person encryption keys make deletion a key-destruction event independent of where ciphertext resides.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Key destruction is an API call with an auditable record.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Key inventory and destruction records are continuous evidence.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Cryptographic erasure plus provider attestation for physical media.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partially: key destruction is verifiable; assurance that no plaintext copy exists requires design review.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Plaintext copies in logs, exports, caches or provider-managed keys that Echelon cannot destroy.
challenge.conventional_cost: High if Echelon owned media; not applicable in cloud.
challenge.alternative_risks: Key loss makes retained data unreadable; provider key escrow could undermine erasure.
supporting_arguments: Matches how cloud storage actually works.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain: some institutions still expect physical destruction language.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Institutions may not accept crypto erasure without explicit policy approval.
Depends on provider key management behavior Echelon does not control.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Deletion from backups
status_rationale: CNV-ARC-005 requires annual restore tests per tenant; UNB-IMM-008 forbids claiming crypto erasure where plaintext persists in backups. Backup retention is not specified.
target_answer: Backups are encrypted under per-tenant keys and expire on a fixed, published cycle (for example 35 days). Deleted data is not surgically removed from backups but becomes unrecoverable when the tenant or person key is destroyed or when the backup expires, whichever is first. If a backup is restored, a replay of erasure and disposition events runs before the restored data is served, so previously deleted records are not reinstated.
current_practice: Not established. Backup design, retention and provider are not selected.
intended_practice: Define backup retention; implement post-restore erasure replay and test it in the annual restore test.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify per-tenant restore testing and prohibit claiming deletion where plaintext remains in backups. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
open_questions: What backup retention period balances recovery needs (RPO, ransomware dwell time) against deletion timeliness?

title: Append-only ledgers and audit logs versus deletion obligations
status_rationale: UNB-DATA-001 makes the authoritative database append-only; SOC2-032 says append-only logs do not exempt personal data from privacy obligations; UNB-DATA-007 proposes an identity vault and cryptographic erasure. The conflict is acknowledged but unresolved.
target_answer: Authoritative events and audit records hold pseudonymous references and ciphertext for personal fields, never plaintext identifiers. Erasure destroys the relevant key; the event chain stays intact because integrity hashes are computed over ciphertext; projections, search indexes and caches are rebuilt and lose the erased values. Echelon reports exactly which classes of personal data remain in retained records (for example pseudonymous fund IDs and amounts) and the legal basis for retaining them.
intended_practice: Decide the hash-over-ciphertext design and the rebuild procedure before the first event schema is frozen.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify an append-only authoritative record together with a reviewed approach to privacy deletion that does not falsely promise deletion of immutable records. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
open_questions: Counsel must resolve jurisdictional retention versus deletion conflicts before production (UNB-DATA-007).

challenge.customer_intent: Customer wants tamper-evident records and lawful deletion at the same time.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Either records can be silently altered, or personal data can never be removed.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Mutable audit logs satisfy deletion but weaken tamper evidence; WORM storage satisfies integrity but blocks deletion.
challenge.legally_required: Some regimes require deletion on request; financial recordkeeping rules require retention; both can apply to the same record.
challenge.contractually_required: DPAs require deletion; regulated customers require immutable audit trails.
challenge.historical_convention: Historically resolved by keeping logs short or by excluding logs from deletion.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Encrypt personal fields under erasable keys and hash ciphertext, so integrity and erasure coexist.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Erasure is a key destruction; projections rebuild automatically.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Chain verification continues after erasure and is reportable.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Hash-over-ciphertext event chain with per-person keys.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes: chain verification and absence of plaintext can be tested.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any plaintext identifier in an event or log line.
challenge.conventional_cost: Low design cost, high conflict cost.
challenge.alternative_risks: Complexity in replay and projections; key management becomes critical.
supporting_arguments: Removes the forced choice between integrity and privacy.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain: auditors and examiners may question whether ciphertext of erased data is still personal data.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Regulators may treat retained ciphertext as personal data.
Implementation complexity in an early-stage company.

title: Recordkeeping obligations of regulated customers (SEC 17a-4, 204-2, bank, IRS, OFAC)
status_rationale: No analysis exists of whether records held in Unbound are required books and records of broker-dealer, RIA or bank customers. CNV-PLT-004 addresses sponsor retention only. UNB-DATA-010 preserves old events through schema evolution.
target_answer: Where a customer's required records reside in Unbound, Echelon supports the customer's obligation: records are preserved in a non-rewriteable form or with a complete time-stamped audit trail of modifications, indexed, producible promptly in readable form, and retained for the customer's required period. For broker-dealer customers, Echelon evaluates whether it can act as the third party providing the undertaking required by Rule 17a-4 and says so explicitly if not. Records remain readable across schema changes through versioned upcasters.
current_practice: Unknown; no analysis or capability exists.
intended_practice: Commission analysis of which customer types would store required records in Unbound; decide whether to support 17a-4 audit-trail alternative.
customer_statement: Echelon has not determined whether Unbound will hold records that SEC- or bank-regulated customers must keep, and makes no claim of Rule 17a-4 or Rule 204-2 compliance.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.

title: Certificates and verifiable evidence of deletion
status_rationale: UNB-TEN-011 requires offboarding with integrity verification and evidence; SOC2-009 requires exportable evidence packages. No certificate format exists.
target_answer: On request and at termination, Echelon issues a signed deletion certificate generated from evidence, not typed by hand: it lists scopes deleted, key destruction event IDs, disposition run IDs, backup expiry dates, subprocessor confirmations received and any data retained under legal hold or legal obligation with the basis. The certificate is a Folio document with an attached machine-readable evidence bundle the customer can verify.
intended_practice: Define certificate content and generate it from erasure and disposition evidence.
